source.shape_note: One row per MEASUREMENT, not per caller: a row reports either one localized source (position, covariance, rank, source id) or one microphone channel's level for the window. Both kinds share the window columns. A localization-only backend names no caller, so this profile declares no caller column, no score and no label map.
source.tool_independence: Roles, never vendor columns. This is the second of two shipped backend templates, written to differ structurally from the first: 3D rather than 2D, a frame named per row, no caller scores, several ranked sources per window, covariance rather than a scalar confidence, and per-channel levels in long rather than wide form.

context.timing_note: Some array localizers re-use the event identifiers of the detector whose calls they localized. Such an identifier is stored verbatim as native_window_id and NEVER interpreted as a VAWLUME detection ID: the window's own times, related by correspondence, are what tie it to an event.

localization.position_note: The frame is named on every source row and resolved per row at intake; it must be a declared 3-dimensional frame when z is reported. Coordinates are stored in the frame's unit exactly as written.

entries.value_semantics: Per-microphone level the array localizer reported for the window; producer={producer}; not normalized, calibrated or compared across channels by VAWLUME

native_attributes.note: A covariance is the positional uncertainty this backend reports. It has no canonical column (contract D15): it is preserved term by term on the estimate, in the producer's units, and nothing derives a scalar confidence from it.

value_semantics.position: Estimated sound-source location; producer={producer}; ranked by the producer among several sources for the window; not a bodypart position
value_semantics.semantics_note: No confidence semantics is declared because this backend reports no scalar confidence; its covariance is preserved as native attributes.

declared_inputs.note: Declare per upstream uncertainty source what the backend used, when known. A template cannot know, so it declares nothing.
